title: Invariant closed subspaces of a smooth atlas descend to closed substacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal X/S$ an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use the fibred-groupoid and 2-fibre-product conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $p:U\to\mathcal X$ be a smooth surjective scheme atlas, with smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and put $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ with projections $s,t$. A closed substack is a strictly full substack whose inclusion is representable and whose pullback to every scheme is a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]; a closed subspace is defined by the same scheme test. Pullback along $p$ gives a bijection between closed substacks $\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathcal X$ and closed subschemes $Z\subseteq U$ satisfying $s^{-1}Z=t^{-1}Z$ as closed subspaces of $R$, with scheme-theoretic inverse images. The corresponding pair satisfies $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z=Z$, and $Z\to\mathcal Z$ is a representable smooth surjective atlas. Each descended $\mathcal Z$ is an algebraic stack.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), closed case; the atlas assertion follows from its cartesian square, and Tag 04YN (lemma-immersion-presentation).

proof.text: For a closed substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$, put $W=U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W$. This is a closed subscheme by its scheme test. An $R$-object includes an isomorphism between its two images in $\mathcal X$; strict fullness makes membership in $\mathcal W$ invariant under it. Thus $s^{-1}W=t^{-1}W$ as subfunctors, hence as closed subspaces, not merely as point subsets.

The etale-stack/atlas descent node makes $\mathcal X$ an fppf stack, so the fppf self-relation and quotient conventions apply. Fix an invariant closed $Z\subseteq U$. The self-relation node gives the groupoid $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$: its arrows are triples $(u,v,\alpha:p(u)\simeq p(v))$. Set $R_Z=s^{-1}Z=t^{-1}Z$. Identity, inversion and composition restrict: an arrow with source in $Z$ has target in $Z$ by invariance; the composite has the source of the first arrow and target of the second. Consequently $R_Z=Z\times_{\mathcal X}Z$, and both maps $R_Z\to Z$ are base changes of the atlas projections $R\to U$. The chartwise calculus makes these maps smooth. The smooth-groupoid quotient theorem gives an algebraic stack $\mathcal Q=[Z/R_Z]$ with smooth surjective scheme atlas $Z\to\mathcal Q$.

source.place: Tag 04YN (lemma-immersion-presentation), restriction of the smooth groupoid.

proof.text: The chartwise calculus makes $p$ flat and locally finitely presented. Its surjectivity is part of the atlas hypothesis, so clause (2) of the fppf-presentation node identifies $[U/R]$ with $\mathcal X$. Apply the cartesian-source criterion to $(Z,R_Z)\to(U,R)$. Its source square is cartesian because $R_Z=Z\times_{U,s}R$; all groupoid operations were restricted in step 2. It follows that $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Q=Z$. The self-relation embedding node, applied to $Z\to\mathcal X$, supplies the same induced map $i:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal X$, fully faithful on every fibre and representable by algebraic spaces because $\mathcal Q$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 04YN, cartesian square; spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 04ZN; algebraic.tex Tags 04WY and 04T4.

proof.text: For a scheme test $T\to\mathcal X$, let $E=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Q$ and $V=T\times_{\mathcal X}U$. These are algebraic spaces by representability of $i$ and of the atlas; $V\to T$ is smooth surjective by the atlas condition. The smooth-cover sections node supplies a jointly surjective etale scheme family $T_a\to T$ lifting to $V$. Associativity of fibre-product tuples and step 3 identify $E\times_TT_a$ with $T_a\times_UZ$. Its projection to $T_a$ is a closed immersion by scheme base change of $Z\to U$. The closed-immersion atlas-locality node, applied to $E\to T$ and this family, proves that $E$ is a closed subscheme of $T$. In particular every scheme test of $i$ is a closed immersion; no scheme-representability of $E$ was presumed.

source.place: Tag 04YN, closedness; use spaces-topologies.tex Tag 0CFV and spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M4 to implement the smooth-cover test.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathcal X$ be the strictly full essential image of $i$: its objects over $T$ are the objects isomorphic to $i(q)$ for some $q\in\mathcal Q(T)$. It is closed under pullback and isomorphism. It is a substack: an etale descent datum in this image lifts to $\mathcal Q$; full faithfulness lifts its overlap arrows uniquely and reflects their cocycle condition. Effectiveness in $\mathcal Q$ then puts the descended object in the image. Isomorphism sheaves are those of $\mathcal X$. The map $\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Z$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective, so it is an equivalence in each fibre, compatible with pullback. Thus the scheme tests from step 4, the diagonal, and the smooth surjective atlas $Z\to\mathcal Q$ give the corresponding tests, diagonal and atlas for $\mathcal Z$. In particular $\mathcal Z$ is algebraic, closed, and has $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z=Z$.

For uniqueness let $\mathcal W_1,\mathcal W_2$ be closed substacks with the same pullback $Z$. For any object $x:T\to\mathcal X$, choose a jointly surjective etale family $T_a\to T$ lifting to the smooth surjective space $T\times_{\mathcal X}U$. It gives maps $u_a:T_a\to U$ and isomorphisms $x|_{T_a}\simeq p(u_a)$. By the specified pullbacks, membership of $x|_{T_a}$ in either $\mathcal W_j$ is equivalent to factorization of $u_a$ through $Z$. Hence these memberships agree. Membership in a strictly full substack is etale-local: local objects with the overlap arrows inherited from $x$ descend in the substack, and the resulting object is isomorphic to $x$ by descent in $\mathcal X$. Therefore $x$ belongs to $\mathcal W_1$ exactly when it belongs to $\mathcal W_2$. Strict fullness then identifies all arrows as well. This proves injectivity, while steps 2--5 prove surjectivity and all atlas and algebraicity assertions.
